p:cNvPr.descr: An illustration of the sequence of events involved in reversible terminator sequencing, as well as involved materials. (a) A sequence of steps for tagging nucleotides and getting them to fluoresce. A vertical DNA strand is shown to the far left, with a key to the left of it. C is shown as a red hexagon, A is shown as a blue hexagon-pentagon combo, T is shown as a yellow hexagon, and G is shown as a green hexagon-pentagon combo. There is an arrow pointing right from the key to the DNA strand. The colors on the strand itself are slightly muted. The left strand has an incomplete sequence, but the sequence of the right strand is TGCATGCATGCA. To the left of this is the first step. It has text that reads, "Add blocked, fluorescently labeled nucleotides." Below this is text reading, "Thymine nucleotide added; fluorescent color observed and recorded." On the unfinished DNA strand on the left, a yellow T has been added. A right arrow with a convergent arrow with the 4 bases above it indicates their addition. Text above reads, "Remove labels and blocking groups; wash; add blocked, labeled nucleotides." On the left side of the DNA, a blue A has been added below the yellow T. Below this there is text that reads, "Adenine nucleotide added; fluorescent color observed and recorded." To the right is an arrow with a convergent arrow that has all 4 bases above it, indicating addition. To the right of this, there is text reading, "Remove labels and blocking groups; wash; add blocked, labeled nucleotides." On the DNA strand, a red C has been added below the blue A. To the left, there is text that reads, "Cytosine nucleotide added; fluorescent color observed and recorded." To the right there is an arrow, with a convergent arrow showing one more addition of all 4 nucleotides. Above this, there is text that reads, "Remove labels and blocking groups; wash; add blocked, labeled nucleotides." Below, on the DNA strand, a green G has been added below the red C. Below this, there is text reading, "Guanine nucleotide added; fluorescent color observed and recorded." (b) Illustration of the results of an Illumia sequencing run. The image is a sequence of 9 black boxes containing dozens of dots, colored red for cytosine, green for guanine, blue for adenine, and yellow for thymine. 2 dots are circled in each box. On the left are two sequences, one on top and one on bottom. The letters are colored according to the nucleotide the represent. The top sequence is TACGGTCTC; the bottom sequence is CCCCCCAGT. The top left corner of the image has text reading, "dNTP incorporated." (c) An image of a light-skinned hand holding a flow cell, which is a clear glass rectangle with parallel horizontal lines running across it. (d) The structure of 3'-O-allyl-dCTP-allyl-Bodipy-FL-510, labeled below. It consists of a pentose ring, bonded up and left to 3 phosphate groups. The pentose ring bonds up and right to a 6-sided ring structure. The ring binds up and left to N, which bonds up and left to C, which double bonds down and left to O and up and right to N. N double bonds up and right to C, which bonds up to NH2, bonds down and right to C, which double bonds down to C and bonds up and left to a long zigzag carbon chain. C bonds down and left to the initial N. The chain begins with C, which bonds right to C, which double bonds right to C, which single bonds right to C. C bonds right to NH, which bonds right to C. C double bonds up to O and bonds right to O. O bonds right to C, which bonds right to C, which has a downward double bond. C bonds right to C, right to C, bonds right to NH, bonds right to C, which double bonds down to O and bonds right to C again. This chain bonds up and right to the blue base. The base consists of 3 rings, a 6-sided ring flanked by 2 5-sided rings. The central 6-sided ring has B at its lower apex, bonded down right & left to F. This is the fluorescent tag. B bonds up and left to N, which bonds up to C, which double bonds up and right to C. C bonds down and right to C, which bonds down to N, which bonds down and left to B. The left 5-sided ring is what actually bonds to the chain. It shares an N with the neighboring 6-sided ring at its bottom right corner. This N double bonds left to C, which bonds up to C, which double bonds up and right to C, which bonds down and right to C, bonds down to N. The right 5-sided ring also shares its lower left N with the 6-sided ring. The N bonds right to C, which bonds right to CH3 and double bonds up to C. C bonds up and left to C, which bonds up to CH3 and double bonds down and left to C. C bonds down to N. (e) The surface of a channel during reversible terminator sequencing. The entire picture is black with tiny, multicolored clusters of dots, resembling sparkles or a night sky.
